key_leads.description: CELM identifies sixteen royalist cipher keys in this volume. No match with the Boswell key is claimed.
key_leads.access: Not found among the 52 Digital Bodleian results for Clarendon; none of the four cipher or seven Boswell results was a relevant key. Separate archival catalogue returned a bot challenge; no challenge bypass attempted.

follow_up_checks.method: Searched OCR for Boswell, Courland/Curland and command/signify formulae.
follow_up_checks.result: No target letter or matching code sequence located. Boswell passages found concern later correspondence. OCR search cannot establish absence from the manuscript collection.

follow_up_checks.source: Calendar of State Papers, Domestic, Charles I, 1641–1643 (1887), pp.507–508
follow_up_checks.result: Calendar reports arms and powder arriving at Dartmouth. No Courland attribution or numerical code; contextual corroboration only. The earlier Nicholas-to-Boswell entry, 15 September 1642, pp.389–390, is SP 16/492/14.

follow_up_checks.source: Theodor Schiemann, Historische Darstellungen und archivalische Studien (1886), pp.183–184
follow_up_checks.result: Describes English correspondence and Wicquefort reports from The Hague, 1641–1676. Archive route only; the inspected discussion supplies no parallel target text. Fraktur OCR is poor.

initial_order_test.status: Unverified structural hypothesis; never used by decoder to assign unknown values.
initial_order_test.rule: Word-code initials are nondecreasing with numerical value. Order within an initial is unrestricted.
limitations: Six working anchors are not a recovered historical codebook.
TWO conflicts with the model; no numeric transcription change is licensed by that conflict.
Within-initial inversions in proposed ARMS/ARE, POWDER/PORT and STATES/SECRET do not refute initial grouping.
